welcome_lead: Time to read graphs and design a fair test — exam-style stretch.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology stretch — calculating rate from time graphs, denaturation as a permanent change, and required-practical fair test planning.
final_note: You calculated mean rate from total ÷ time, found instantaneous rate from a graph's steepest gradient, explained why denaturation is permanent, and planned a one-variable fair test.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mean rate = total quantity ÷ total time. Units e.g. cm³/s or mg/min.

Example: 24 cm³ of gas made in 60 s → mean rate = 0.4 cm³/s.

Instantaneous rate = gradient at a single point. The steepest part of the curve is the highest rate — usually right at the start, before substrate runs low.

A flat curve (plateau) means the reaction is over.

Cooling a slow reaction simply lets it warm up again and resume.

But if you cook an enzyme past its optimum, the bonds holding its shape break.

The active site is permanently a different shape. Substrate can no longer fit. Cooling does not bring it back.

Think: a boiled egg can't be un-boiled.

Required practical thinking — change one thing only.

- Independent variable: the thing you change (e.g. pH).
- Dependent variable: the thing you measure (e.g. time for iodine to stop going blue-black with amylase + starch).
- Control variables: keep constant — temperature, enzyme volume, substrate volume, substrate concentration.

Repeat each value and take a mean. Plot a graph. The optimum is where rate is highest.

mcqs.q: On a curve showing product against time, where is the rate fastest?
options: At the flat plateau
At the steepest part (start)
At the very end
At the x-axis

mcqs.q: Why can't a denatured enzyme be restored by cooling?
options: Cooling kills it
The active site's shape change is permanent
It becomes a substrate
It runs out of energy

mcqs.q: What happens to an enzyme when it is denatured?
options: The enzyme has been completely broken into amino acids.
The enzyme has died because enzymes are alive.
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
Its tertiary structure (3D shape) changes, particularly the active site, so it can no longer bind substrate effectively.

mcqs.q: Why are enzymes specific to certain substrates?
options: Enzymes choose their substrate based on which one is most common in the cell.
The enzyme has been completely broken into amino acids.
Only substrates with complementary shape and chemistry to the active site can bind effectively.
Each enzyme can react with any substrate, but works fastest with one type.
Respiration means breathing — inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.
A series of chemical reactions in cells that break down glucose to release energy as ATP.
The enzyme has been completely broken into amino acids.
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
